title: 走神问卷（5题）

rights.basis: Original authors publish complete MWQ wording in Study 1 and Table 1, under article CC BY linked to version 3.0. No separate exclusion for MWQ form. Footnote transparently identifies items 3 and 4 adapted from MAAS; original MAAS is not being republished.
rights.attribution: Mrazek et al. (2013), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2013.00560; retain article/CC-BY3 links and identify Chinese project adaptation.

references.citation: Mrazek, M. D., Phillips, D. T., Franklin, M. S., Broadway, J. M., & Schooler, J. W. (2013). Young and restless: validation of the Mind-Wandering Questionnaire (MWQ) reveals disruptive impact of mind-wandering for youth. Frontiers in Psychology, 4, 560.
references.role: Original authors, exact five items, 6-point response anchors, Study 1 validation, adolescent studies, CC-BY3 link

instructions.en: Project administration instruction: Rate how frequently each statement applies to you.
instructions.zh: 请根据平时的情况，选择以下每句话发生的频繁程度。
instructions.timeframe: general tendency; no fixed recall window
instructions.provenance: Administration wording composed by project; exact item and anchor wording from original.

items.en: I have difficulty maintaining focus on simple or repetitive work
items.zh: 做简单或重复的工作时，我很难保持专注。

items.en: While reading, I find I haven't been thinking about the text and must therefore read it again
items.zh: 阅读时，我发现自己并没有在想文字的内容，因此不得不重新读一遍。

items.en: I do things without paying full attention
items.zh: 我做事时没有把注意力完全放在上面。

items.en: I find myself listening with one ear, thinking about something else at the same time
items.zh: 我发现自己一边听着，一边在想别的事情。

items.en: I mind-wander during lectures or presentations
items.zh: 听课或听报告时，我会走神。

scoring.basis: Unidimensional 5-item form and Tables 2–3 report MWQ means on response metric (3.68 and 3.44). Project uses equal-weight mean of all 5 items; original prose does not separately state an explicit MWQ aggregation formula. Do not confuse thought-probe mean with MWQ scoring.
scoring.missingProjectPolicy: All five responses required; no imputation; no score/report for incomplete response set.

report.title: 看看注意力什么时候悄悄拐了弯
report.summary: 这份问卷关注做事时，思绪转向其他内容的频繁程度。走神不等于懒惰，也不能据此判断有没有注意力障碍。
report.interpretation: 回答反映的是您对平时走神的感受；平均分越高，表示您报告这些情况更常发生。它不是某一节课的专注监测，也不直接代表学习能力。
report.dailyExample: 比如眼睛还在读下一行，脑子却已经想到另一件事；发现后回头重读，就是一种常见情境。
report.reflection: 想想最近一次走神：当时任务是否单调、是否疲劳，或者是否有事情一直挂在心上？
report.smallAction: 下一次开始任务前，先写下眼前这一小步要做什么。发现走神时，记下待会再想的事，再把注意力轻轻带回当前一步。
report.caveat: 本中文为独立工作译稿，尚未验证，不用于诊断、学生筛选或能力排名。原研究没有提供可直接用于个人分级的界线。

changesNotice: 本项目据原作者2013年MWQ发布文字独立翻译并编写通俗反馈。保留五题顺序与六级频率锚点；尚非经验证的中文版本，原作者未背书。
sourceDiscrepancies: Item 5 Study 1 prose says lectures or presentations; Table 1 has lectures of presentations. Preserve prose wording as questionnaire form; record table typo rather than silently rewriting source.
Study 3 prose says 106 female high-school students; Table 2 caption says N=156. Neither treated as population norm.
thresholdPolicy: No validated diagnostic thresholds or low/medium/high bands in original. Do not use sample mean/SD as cutoffs or ADHD indicators.

sampleContext.study3: California female high-school sample; paper inconsistent n=106 prose vs156 table; no normative inference
sampleContext.scope: English original has adolescent evidence; project Chinese translation has no local validation. English validation does not validate Chinese/K12 deployment.
